races.name: Irish EBF Median Sires Series Maiden
Irish Stallion Farms EBF Maiden

runners_data.name: Basilano
runners_data.note: Shaped well over 6f on Soft earlier in career but OR 120 flatters given three consecutive finishing positions of 8-8; trainer Watson has had no winners in 14 days from three runners, and this horse's natural hold-up style is compromised here as a true rear-division runner operating in a tighter midfield slot than preferred.

runners_data.name: In The Gloaming
runners_data.note: Placed sixth on Good at 5f previously and has course-distance experience worth noting, but Gary Carroll's mount has finished no better than fifth in five starts and Oliver's stable is light on recent form; a natural hold-up runner who will find the redistributed midfield position constraining in a race where closers face a congested path.

runners_data.name: Banish Misfortune
runners_data.note: Four-year-old with a string of 0800 form and a "fades in finish" flag who has twice run on Good ground without troubling the placed horses; Kyne sends this out only 17 days after last start, but as a genuine rear-tracker now mapped to midfield, the style mismatch is a real concern at this trip.

runners_data.name: Forza Magico
runners_data.note: Two runs, two placed efforts at 6f on Good for Feane — the step back to 5f is a slight query but the profile of a horse that races prominently and stays competitive suits this pace map well; Sheridan takes the ride on a yard with four runners in the past fortnight and this represents the most straightforward prominent threat to Otsana.

runners_data.name: Gaineamh Min
runners_data.note: Single run to date, finished 12th of field over 6f on Good, and carries a "fades in finish" flag; Byrne's yard has had no runners in the 14-day window, and this lightly raced three-year-old holds an unknown ceiling on just one start at further.

runners_data.name: Kiss Don't Tell
runners_data.note: Ran second at 5f on Yielding for McLoughlin who has one winner from 23 runners in 14 days, and the prominent profile suits this race shape; the "fades in finish" tag is a concern over the final furlong but the ability to get close to the pace gives this runner a better route to competitiveness than most in this field.

runners_data.name: Orellana
runners_data.note: Single run over 8f on Good, finishing tenth — both lightly raced and stepping back in trip to 5f; Rutledge rides for Rogers and the unknown trip, fade tendency, and minimal form make this one of the more opaque profiles in the race.

runners_data.name: Osterode
runners_data.note: Fourth and fifth from two starts at 5f on Good and Standard, wearing a visor today which could sharpen the response early; McCreery's stable has been in strong form with seven winners from 22 runners in 14 days and Declan McDonogh is an excellent booking, making this one of the more interesting hold-up types if the visor effect is significant.

runners_data.name: Otsana
runners_data.note: The sole confirmed front-runner in the race, W J Lee in the saddle for Twomey, and one prior run of fifth over 7f on Good suggests the switch to 5f with the lead to herself is a fresh opportunity; an uncontested lead on a flat track in a maiden shapes this as her ideal tactical scenario.

runners_data.name: Sarfarcat
runners_data.note: Form reads 0-060 with a best finish of sixth from seven runs, primarily over 7-8f trips, and this drop to 5f is uncharted territory; a hold-up runner who has never finished better than sixth, with the "fades in finish" flag, faces a tough ask to reverse those trends here.

runners_data.name: Sassy Boom
runners_data.note: Returning from 182 days off, wearing a tongue-tie, and has four consecutive finishes of 8-10-12-10 — the layoff combined with the fade tendency and the hold-up style in a compressed field makes this a difficult proposition; O'Connell's yard has had no runners in the 14-day window.

runners_data.name: Tudor Flame
runners_data.note: Debutant for Feane who also runs Forza Magico, carrying an unknown going profile and no form to assess; McGettigan takes a 5lb claim which could be meaningful if the horse has ability, but the complete absence of form history makes this entirely speculative.

runners_data.name: Famed Again
runners_data.note: Five-year-old with a career-best fifth at 7f on Good but otherwise finishing well out of contention; McLoughlin's yard has one winner from two runners in 14 days, and while the style is naturally suited to holding up, this horse's redistribution to a midfield slot means it won't get the cleanest run in a 14-runner field over a short trip.

runners_data.name: White Smoke
runners_data.note: Has placed once from ten runs, with form at 5f on Good (seventh, fourth) suggesting the trip is correct; a natural hold-up type whose best chance lies in traffic-free running from midfield, but the STYLE_FIT flag and redistribution context mean a repeat of that fourth at 5f on Good would represent an improvement on trend.

races.paceDynamic: Otsana is the sole confirmed front-runner in this 14-runner maiden, and with no other horse credibly capable of disputing the early lead, W J Lee can dictate a sustainable, controlled pace from the front on a flat 5f track at Down Royal on Good ground. The field contains a heavy concentration of hold-up and midfield types — Basilano, Banish Misfortune, In The Gloaming, Famed Again and White Smoke are all true rear-division horses who have been redistributed forward on the map because there is simply no room for them all at the back — meaning the genuine closers will be bunched together and unable to express their natural style cleanly. Forza Magico and Kiss Don't Tell represent the main prominent challengers who can at least track Otsana through the race, giving the front two zones the strongest profile. This race shape strongly favours a front-running or prominent-pressing profile: Otsana controls the tempo uncontested, the hold-up brigade will face traffic and positional compromise, and those who can sit just behind the pace and strike approaching the final furlong are best placed.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Otsana Leads Unchallenged
scenarios.trigger: If Otsana breaks cleanly and establishes a clear lead within the first furlong, setting a controlled but not slow pace.
scenarios.body: Otsana dictates every yard of the race on her own terms, and W J Lee can produce her sprint at the two-furlong pole before any hold-up horse can close the gap on this short 5f trip. The flat, straight nature of Down Royal means a horse in front with a clear gallop can be very hard to reel in, and the compressed hold-up cluster will struggle to find a clean passage.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Presser Strikes
scenarios.trigger: If a prominent runner tracks Otsana closely enough to pounce in the final furlong as the pace fractionally dips.
scenarios.body: Forza Magico, with two placings from two starts on Good ground, is best positioned to press the pace and strike late if Otsana's sprint capacity is limited, while Kiss Don't Tell from a prominent position could also mount a challenge. This scenario rewards horses that can sit within a length of the leader and produce a clean switch to the outside in the closing stages.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Burst Arrives Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is genuinely strong enough to string the field out and create a proper target for closers.
scenarios.body: Osterode with visor headgear and a fourth placing on Good ground represents the most credible hold-up threat, while White Smoke has shown consistency at this trip on Good ground and might find daylight late. However, given the redistribution congestion among true closers and the expectation of a controlled rather than fast pace, this scenario is structurally disadvantaged and depends on an unusual pace collapse at the front.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Messy Scrappy Finish
scenarios.trigger: If the large 14-runner field causes interference, slow early pace, or a false start disrupts natural positions.
scenarios.body: With 14 maidens over 5f, a bunched early phase could see multiple horses lose position or check, creating a chaotic straight where momentum rather than tactical position wins out. Tudor Flame, the debutant with unknown going profile, could emerge as a beneficiary if natural ability overrides tactical disadvantage.

watchPoints.text: Otsana is the only confirmed front-runner in 14 — watch the draw and W J Lee's break from the gates: if she is away cleanly, the entire race shape is set and she could prove very hard to catch over 5f with no pace pressure.

Osterode's visor is fitted for the first time today — watch whether McCreery's booking of Declan McDonogh and the headgear combination produces an unexpected early jump in performance, as this horse has shown a respectable form ceiling at this trip.

The cluster of redistributed hold-up horses — Basilano, Banish Misfortune, In The Gloaming, Famed Again and White Smoke — will all be looking for a run in the same part of the track in the straight; watch for traffic and checking issues that could affect multiple runners simultaneously.

Tudor Flame is a debutant for a yard that also runs Forza Magico — watch the market movement on this horse in the final 30 minutes before the off, as significant support from a stable with stable information could signal unexpected readiness.

Forza Magico drops from 6f to 5f having placed twice on Good — watch whether Sheridan positions this one just off Otsana's shoulder from the outset, as the ability to press the pace cleanly is the key tactical requirement for any horse to challenge the front-runner at this trip.

races.name: Grant Thornton Nursery Handicap

runners_data.name: Someday Somewhere
runners_data.note: Four runs of consistent placed form including a third at this trip on Good, sits naturally prominent, Jack Kearney's 3lb claim is useful and Stephen Thorne is 1/4 in the last 14 days; best profile in this race shape.

runners_data.name: Romance
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse but has run respectably at 7f and 8f on Good, Andrew Slattery takes the ride, tongue-tie fitted; went 6/7f on Good last time and was beaten a manageable distance, form holds up at this level.
runners_data.comment: Romance shapes as a strong threat on our rating, ranked top of the field, and she has experience of today's trip and conditions; the risk is that she has been winless in her last three starts.

runners_data.name: Arizonaneargalway
runners_data.note: Consistent record of finishing in the pack at 7f on Good — four runs at similar going, four times out of the frame; flagged for fading in the finish and Mel Sheridan's 7lb claim does not offset the lack of any finishing kick.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last four starts, with a string of eighths and unplaced efforts, Arizonaneargalway is hard to fancy at 133 lb from stall 10, and a trainer striking at just 4% recently does little to inspire confidence, despite her experience over today's trip and going.

runners_data.name: Summer Sent You
runners_data.note: A true hold-up horse pushed into a midfield map position because the rear is overcrowded; STYLE_FIT of 0.90 signals she is racing out of her natural role, three runs at this trip on Good all ended outside the places, and the fade flag is a concern.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last three starts, Summer Sent You has at least run over today's trip and going, and a fifth on her most recent outing edges ahead of two unplaced efforts before it; the 131 lb burden from stall seven is the obvious concern.

runners_data.name: Thelymitra
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last three starts, Thelymitra has run over today's trip and going before, and 38 days between runs at least suggests she returns fresh; however, her recent unplaced effort and a speed rating of 52 temper expectations from stall three carrying 131 lb.

runners_data.name: Fine Line
runners_data.note: Four runs at this trip and further on Good, best effort was a 4th at 8f; a true closer dropped into midfield on the map because there is no room at the rear — the STYLE_FIT discount applies and Reese Holohan's 7lb claim does not compensate for an out-of-position run.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last five starts and with a trainer operating at just 4% in the past fortnight, Fine Line faces an uphill task, though she has experience over today's trip and going, and a rating of 75 suggests she holds more ability than her recent finishes imply.

runners_data.name: Elyatta
runners_data.note: Blinkers on, ran just six days ago for Noel Meade who is 1/28 in 14 days, W J Lee is a significant booking; finished 4th last time at 7f on Good, but is another genuine hold-up horse squeezed into a midfield slot — the headgear change is the one thing to respect here.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last four starts and drawn in stall nine carrying 129 lb, Elyatta does at least have experience over today's trip and going, and a rating of 76 offers encouragement — though a trainer striking at just four per cent is the concern.

runners_data.name: Dear Theodosia
runners_data.note: Redistributed to the front as the most likely pace-setter despite being a natural prominent type; blinkers fitted, Ben Coen rides, but her three runs on Good have all resulted in finishes of 9th, 12th and 11th — low STYLE_FIT of 0.80 and weak form make her a fragile leader.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last three starts, with a ninth and two unplaced efforts, Dear Theodosia arrives with a trainer badly out of form at 4% and ranked near the foot of the field on our figures, making her very hard to fancy despite the experience over today's trip and going.

runners_data.name: Ballymackney
runners_data.note: Blinkers on for Noel Meade, Chris Hayes in the saddle, but returning after 43 days and pushed into midfield despite being a true closer; best efforts were 7th at 5f and 9th at 8f — the longer layoff and out-of-role position are both negatives.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last three starts and held up by a trainer in lean form at just 4% over the past fortnight, Ballymackney does at least return with distance and going experience and a rating of 68 offering some encouragement, though she faces an uphill task from stall 8 carrying 123 lb.

runners_data.name: Rathbran Lady
runners_data.note: Michael Mulvany is 2/13 in 14 days which is the best recent trainer strike rate in this field; however she is a genuine hold-up horse mapped to midfield, has only finished 7th, 10th and 12th in three starts, and the STYLE_FIT discount applies — trainer form is the sole positive angle.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last three starts — including a seventh and two unplaced efforts — Rathbran Lady heads into this in poor heart, and our rating ranks her last of ten runners; she does at least return eight days fresh and has run over today's distance and going before.

races.paceDynamic: Dear Theodosia is the only horse mapped to the front, though she is a redistributed prominent type rather than a natural front-runner, and with a STYLE_FIT of 0.80 she is likely to set a modest, uncontested pace on Good ground over 7f at Down Royal. Someday Somewhere and Romance sit closest behind as the most naturally prominent runners, giving this race a compressed, processional shape where the early tempo is unlikely to be severe. The field is saturated with hold-up types — Summer Sent You, Fine Line, Elyatta, Ballymackney and Rathbran Lady are all genuine closers redistributed into midfield positions because there simply is not enough pace ahead of them to allow everyone to settle at the rear. With a single, reluctant front-runner and a long string of horses forced to race closer than they want, this race shape favours horses who can sit prominently or just off the pace and quicken from a good position in the straight, rather than true closers who will struggle to find clear daylight from a muddled midfield.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Prominent Types Dominate
scenarios.trigger: If Dear Theodosia sets a steady, uncontested pace and the race develops as a positional contest from the home turn.
scenarios.body: Someday Somewhere and Romance, sitting closest to the action without being trapped wide, are best placed to pick up when the tempo increases in the final two furlongs; the lack of genuine pace suits those who travel smoothly in the first half of the race rather than those charging from behind.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Late Rush From Midfield
scenarios.trigger: If Dear Theodosia quickens early enough to create a falsely strong pace that causes the prominent group to tire in the final furlong.
scenarios.body: The redistributed midfield closers — Summer Sent You, Fine Line or Elyatta — would then have a legitimate run at the leaders, though their out-of-role positioning makes this genuinely less likely; this scenario requires conditions that the current race shape does not strongly support.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Pace Collapses Early
scenarios.trigger: If Dear Theodosia is unable to hold the lead past halfway and the field compresses into a slowly-run, bunched sprint finish.
scenarios.body: Horses with a high turn-of-foot in a tight finish would benefit, and Thelymitra and Elyatta, who have shown some ability to finish off a race when the race is run at a level tempo, could capitalise; however, the widespread "fades in finish" flags across this field limit confidence in any dramatic late flourish.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Front Runner Holds On
scenarios.trigger: If Dear Theodosia, untroubled on the lead, finds a low enough tempo to conserve energy and simply outstay a disorganised midfield pack.
scenarios.body: Despite her STYLE_FIT penalty and poor recent form figures, a truly uncontested lead on Good ground over 7f could allow her to set her own fractions and hold on; the absence of any horse willing to chase her aggressively makes this a small but genuine possibility.

watchPoints.text: Elyatta and Ballymackney — both trained by Noel Meade and wearing blinkers; if the headgear change sparks improvement from either, the W J Lee/Chris Hayes bookings give them a tactical advantage in a muddled midfield.

Dear Theodosia's early pace — if she is unable to hold the front past the 4f pole, the entire race shape collapses and the processional tempo scenario breaks down, reshuffling chances for everyone behind her.

Summer Sent You, Fine Line and Rathbran Lady are all true closers racing out of position; if they drift to the rear from their mapped midfield slots, the back straight could see a long, strung-out tail that makes late headway almost impossible on Good ground.

Rathbran Lady's trainer Michael Mulvany strikes at 2/13 in the past 14 days — the best in-form handler in this race; worth monitoring in the market for any confidence signal even if her form figures are poor.

Thelymitha returns for JP O'Brien after 38 days off wearing a tongue-tie; O'Brien's string is capable of winning first time out of a break and this is the one runner where the layoff angle is worth tracking against market moves.

races.name: Grant Thornton Ulster Cesarewitch Handicap

runners_data.name: Ragmans Corner
runners_data.note: Won over 17f on Good last time out and has placed twice in five similar-going runs; hold-up operator who has proven he can produce a decisive late run in the right pace scenario, and this controlled tempo suits if he can travel close enough.
runners_data.comment: Ragmans Corner won last time out and has experience of today's going, making him the one to beat on our ratings here; he was third four starts back and again five starts back, and a return to that consistency under 140 lb looks well within reach.

runners_data.name: Boxing Great
runners_data.note: Last-time-out winner over 15f on Good, wears a tongue-tie today; true hold-up runner who needs things to happen around him, and the tepid Trubshaw-set tempo may not generate enough pace to unlock his best finish.
runners_data.comment: Boxing Great won last time out and also took a race five starts back, so he arrives in decent heart, though a pair of mid-field finishes either side of that earlier success give pause; has run over today's trip and going, and 134 lb is the test of whether that recent winning form translates.

runners_data.name: Happy Jacky
runners_data.note: Prominent racer at 12 years old who has form in demanding chases and long-distance flat handicaps; Good ground suits well, and his willingness to race close to the pace makes him one of the few who is naturally suited to the anticipated race shape.

runners_data.name: Trubshaw
runners_data.note: The sole confirmed front-runner, recent winner over 14f on Good for Henry De Bromhead and a young claimer; wears a hood, has the pace asset of an uncontested lead, but her stamina over 2m2½f remains unproven.
runners_data.comment: Trubshaw landed a win 14 days ago but his wider recent form is inconsistent at best, and our rating of 65 leaves him well below the top of this field; familiarity with today's going is slim consolation when ranked 15th of 17.

runners_data.name: Zoffman
runners_data.note: Flagged as fading in the finish; ran just four days ago which is a significant fitness concern in a stamina test of this length, and his record shows a pattern of threatening without converting.
runners_data.comment: Zoffman returns just four days after his last outing, and while he has run over today's going before, he is yet to win in his last five starts and his trainer is in poor form; third two starts back is the best he can offer at present.

runners_data.name: Feud
runners_data.note: Has been out of form recently with a run of poor finishes; hold-up style and Good-ground form over long trips gives him a theoretical chance, but consistency has been absent.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last four starts, Feud nevertheless catches the eye with our rating of 80 ranking him second among 17 rivals, and he returns on a quick 15-day turnaround with going experience in his favour; the concern is a recent form line that offers little encouragement.

runners_data.name: Golden Temple
runners_data.note: Won over 20f on Good and placed over 22f — the trip and ground are squarely in his wheelhouse — but his natural rear-of-field style is compromised by the redistribution effect in this hold-up-heavy field.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last four starts, Golden Temple's sole encouragement is a second four starts back, though a struggling trainer (1/28 in the last 14 days) and a hefty 131 lb to carry are real headwinds; has run over today's going, which offers some small comfort.

runners_data.name: Sign From Above
runners_data.note: Wears a hood and has been placing at a lower frequency recently with a string of mid-pack finishes; a genuine hold-up horse pushed into a midfield role by the weight of similar runners, tempering confidence in his chance here.
runners_data.comment: Sign From Above has been winless in his last five starts, with a best recent effort of third, and at 131 lb he faces a stiff task — though he has run over today's trip and going before and a speed rating of 86 offers some encouragement returning after 37 days off.

runners_data.name: Way Down South
runners_data.note: A consistent mid-division finisher rather than a winner, with no wins from nine Good-ground starts; his natural closer's style is squeezed by the field configuration and his flat recent record is unpromising.
runners_data.comment: Way Down South carries 131 lb yet our rating of 78 puts him 7lb ahead of his official rating of 71, and he returns on familiar going after a sharp 20-day turnaround; the concern is that he has been winless in his last five starts and needs to find improvement in the finish.

runners_data.name: Banana Three
runners_data.note: Wears a hood and has placed multiple times over distances up to 20f on Good; his true closing style is compromised by the high density of hold-up horses in the field, and he has not won in this going.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts, Banana Three does bring going experience and a place among the mid-division on our figures, yet a 49-day absence, a taxing 130 lb to carry, and a trainer firing at just 5% recently are notable headwinds.

runners_data.name: Cozone
runners_data.note: Nine-year-old with course experience and historic wins over similar trips on Good and Soft; ran just four days ago and his true hold-up style will be tested by a field that forces him forward earlier than ideal.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts and back out just four days later, Cozone faces a stiff ask off 130 lb, though he has run over today's going before and our rating of 77 suggests there may be a little more to work with than his recent figures imply.

runners_data.name: Alba Chiara
runners_data.note: Young four-year-old stepping up sharply in trip from 13f to 18f; form has been poor in recent starts and there is a significant experience and stamina question at this distance.
runners_data.comment: Alba Chiara showed a glimpse of promise with a second in her recent form but has been winless in her last five starts, and 49 days off the track is a fitness query, though she has run over today's trip and going and our rating of 76 suggests she retains some ability.

runners_data.name: Gangster Granny
runners_data.note: Exceptional record over 22f on Good ground — four wins from five at that trip on this going — and her genuinely strong stayer profile stands out; held up naturally but the redistribution effect means she cannot fully exploit the deep position that suits her best.
runners_data.comment: Beaten in her last two starts and ranked thirteenth of seventeen on our figures, Gangster Granny is hard to fancy at the weights, though she does have going experience to call on and her win three starts back shows she retains ability on her day.

runners_data.name: Yogini
runners_data.note: Three-year-old on just a third career start, form capped at 12f, stepping up to 18f in a competitive 17-runner handicap; inexperience and trip concerns make this a significant ask.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last three starts and ranked last on our figures, Yogini looks to have plenty to prove here, though he has run over today's going before and the 23-day break may have him fresh enough to improve on an unplaced effort last time out.

runners_data.name: Sanctity Of Space
runners_data.note: Unknown running style and no jockey declared — both are material uncertainties at this stage; has run well over 16f on Good in the past with a second, but form has been inconsistent.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last five starts, Sanctity Of Space does at least bring going experience to the table and a respectable speed rating, though her recent placed-at-best efforts and a 37-day absence make confidence hard to muster.

runners_data.name: Deralo Ir
runners_data.note: Young four-year-old whose best form has come at 10-13f on Soft; stepping up to 18f on Good is a double question mark, and his profile does not obviously suit the anticipated race dynamics.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts, with a sixth last time out and a runner-up effort earlier in that sequence, Deralo Ir is rated well below the field on our figures and faces a stiff ask here, though he has run over today's going before and returns on a reasonable 17-day break.

runners_data.name: Cooley's Mist
runners_data.note: Last-time-out winner over 13f on Good, progressive handicapper; the step to 18f is the key unknown, though Good ground and recent form are positives if the stamina question is answered.
runners_data.comment: Cooley's Mist matched his official mark on our figures and ranks fourteenth of seventeen in the field, making him hard to fancy despite a second last time out and a win three starts back, though he does bring going experience to the table.

races.paceDynamic: Trubshaw is the lone confirmed front-runner in a field of 17 over 2m2½f on Good ground at Down Royal, and with no genuine rival willing to press her early, she is set to dictate a controlled, measured gallop from the outset. The pace will be sustainable rather than searching — a steady tempo through the early stages before the race develops turning for home, which classically suits horses who can travel through the race rather than those who need a true test of stamina from the front. The field contains an unusually high concentration of hold-up types — Golden Temple, Sign From Above, Way Down South, Banana Three, Cozone, Alba Chiara, Gangster Granny, Deralo Ir and Cooley's Mist are all genuine rear-of-field operators who cannot all occupy their natural position, meaning several will race closer to the pace than intended and the rear of the field may be more congested than usual. This race shape — a lone controlled leader setting an honest but uncontested tempo over a stamina trip — most favours prominent racers and mid-division horses who can track the gallop efficiently and produce a sustained late run, rather than true closers who need a stronger pace to set them alight.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Trubshaw Controls, Prominent Win
scenarios.trigger: If Trubshaw is allowed to dictate a steady, uncontested gallop and the race develops into a stamina test from the home turn.
scenarios.body: Trubshaw sets her own fractions unchallenged and the prominent horses who track her — Happy Jacky and Ragmans Corner — are best placed to pounce late; the steady tempo rewards those who travel economically rather than those deep in the field waiting for a strong pace that never comes.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Front-Runner Steals It
scenarios.trigger: If Trubshaw's uncontested lead stretches far enough that she builds an insurmountable advantage and the hold-up runners are caught flat-footed.
scenarios.body: With no rival to pressure her, Trubshaw can effectively time her own race, conserving energy through the long galloping stretch before picking up again in the straight; a strongly-run finish to an otherwise steady race can leave deep closers with too much ground to make up in the short run-in.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Midfield Hold-Up Rallies Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is genuinely honest enough in the middle stages to soften the leader and allow the redistributed hold-up horses to find their stride from further back.
scenarios.body: Gangster Granny is one of the few genuine hold-up horses with a strong recent record over this sort of trip and going, and Ragmans Corner has placed from off the pace over course-relevant distances; however, most redistributed horses here are racing out of their natural position, which tempers confidence in this outcome.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Compressed Finish, Front Swamped
scenarios.trigger: If the pace collapses entirely in the straight and a wall of horses from mid-division makes late ground simultaneously.
scenarios.body: A very slow tempo can paradoxically produce a chaotic sprint finish in a large-field handicap, catching the leader cold; but with most hold-up horses forced forward and the field spread across the track, a clean late surge from the deepest closers is the least likely outcome in this configuration.

watchPoints.text: Gangster Granny — four wins from five over 22f on Good ground is an outstanding record for this trip and going, but watch whether she can find her natural deep position given the redistribution effect; if she travels well in the final quarter-mile, she becomes the most dangerous late runner in the race.

Trubshaw's sectionals through the first mile — if she is allowed to coast at a very slow pace, she may be almost impossible to catch late, but if the mid-division horses close early, she becomes vulnerable to being swallowed up in the straight.
Zoffman ran only four days ago and is flagged as fading in the finish; monitor for signs of fatigue in the final two furlongs, as this could cause interference in a compressed finish with 17 runners.

Yogini and Alba Chiara are both young horses stepping well beyond their proven trip; watch the early exchanges to see whether they are settled by their jockeys or whether they use up energy trying to find a position in a big field.
Cozone also ran four days ago — two runners with minimal recovery time in a 2m2½f stamina test on Good ground is worth flagging for pace collapse risk in the straight if both fade simultaneously.

races.name: Children's Heartbeat Trust Apprentice Handicap

runners_data.name: Solomon Coop
runners_data.note: Hold-up performer returning from 259 days off, which is a substantial absence concern; similar-going form reads 1W2P across 15 runs so the ground is not an issue, but the layoff and a tendency to race at the rear in a field where rear berths will be crowded makes his task harder.

runners_data.name: Areana
runners_data.note: Won twice at 10f on good for this yard and the trip looks ideal, but 355 days off is a serious flag; a genuine hold-up horse who will find herself racing closer to midfield than she prefers because the rear is oversubscribed, and her chance depends heavily on whether the layoff has left her sharp enough.
runners_data.comment: Areana has won twice in her last four starts, including back-to-back victories two and three runs back, and she has experience over today's distance and going — but a 355-day absence and an unplaced effort last time out are clear concerns heading into this.

runners_data.name: Darkdeserthighway
runners_data.note: The tongue-tie and a recent run 17 days ago keep freshness concerns low, and 9/15 similar-going qualifiers suggest the ground suits; a horse that wants to race from the back but will be squeezed into a midfield position by weight of numbers, which blunts the profile in what looks a steadily-run race.
runners_data.comment: Darkdeserthighway shapes as an appealing each-way contender off an official mark of 68, with a second two starts back suggesting she retains ability, and her experience over today's distance and going is a plus; fourth last time out and a 17-day gap leave her close to peak fitness stepping out from stall 17.

runners_data.name: Doctor Grace
runners_data.note: Won at 12f on good and placed at 10f on Tapeta, so the trip and ground combination are well within range; the hood is noted, and his last two runs show back-to-back 11th-place finishes, so he needs to rediscover form — the held-up style at least means he won't be inconvenienced by the slow early pace as much as some.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last three starts — including an unseating — and ranked near the foot of the field on our figures, Doctor Grace is hard to fancy at this level; she has run over today's trip and going, and a break of 72 days at least leaves the freshness angle open.

runners_data.name: Sinbad My Dad
runners_data.note: Second over 11f on good last time out and placed at 10f on the same surface — both positive indicators for today; a hold-up horse who ran only 12 days ago so freshness is fine, and among the backmarkers he has arguably the most relevant recent course-and-trip form profile.
runners_data.comment: Sinbad My Dad arrives on the back of a runner-up finish last time out, which offers encouragement, though he remains winless in his last six starts and carries 139 lb from stall 13, making life harder again here.

runners_data.name: Solomon
runners_data.note: Flagged for fading in the finish and the historic data shows six finishes between 6th and 16th; a genuine hold-up horse mapped to midfield through field congestion, and the tendency to weaken late in a race likely to be run at a controlled pace makes his prospects slim.
runners_data.comment: Solomon is ranked second of seventeen in the field on a speed rating of 77, giving connections genuine cause for optimism, and he has run over today's distance and going before; the main concern is a winless recent spell and 196 days off the track.

runners_data.name: Berto Ramirez
runners_data.note: Consistent placer over 12f on good (three 4ths in last four on similar ground) but has never won on good; forced off his natural hold-up berth into a midfield slot by the volume of closers in this field, and the 20-day freshness is fine — the concern is simply that he needs stronger pace than A Pretty Penny is likely to generate.
runners_data.comment: Berto Ramirez has run over today's trip and going before, and a rating of 73 offers him some appeal against this field, yet he is winless in his last five starts and those three consecutive fourths suggest he finds a way to be competitive without quite seeing it out.

runners_data.name: Daonethatgotaway
runners_data.note: Tongue-tie noted; ran 17 days ago and has no wins or places on good ground from five qualifying runs, which is a material concern for today's conditions; a natural hold-up horse compelled to race more prominently than usual, and the combined flags of going form and no finish-line punch make this a difficult race.
runners_data.comment: Daonethatgotaway arrives here 17 days fresh and has run over today's trip and going, yet winless in his last six starts and drawing stall 12 under 137 lb, he heads into this as a mid-division prospect with a second five starts back his lone recent highlight.

runners_data.name: Hexagonal
runners_data.note: Tongue-tie worn, two wins at 10f on good from nine starts on similar ground (9/15 qualifiers), and returned to form with a win 17 days ago (601071 sequence); styles himself as a prominent racer, which is precisely the profile that suits a steadily-run race where A Pretty Penny controls the tempo — one of the most interesting contenders in this shape.
runners_data.comment: Hexagonal won last time out and has run over today's trip and going, giving him a solid platform from stall one carrying 137 lb, but his trainer's dire recent strike rate of just one winner from 28 gives obvious cause for caution.

runners_data.name: Enchanted Lady
runners_data.note: Hood worn, last five runs show finishes of 4th-9th with no win; a genuine hold-up horse relocated to midfield by field congestion, and while the 17-day turnaround is positive, only 4 of 6 similar-going runs show any competitiveness — the profile doesn't suit a race where closers will struggle to find space.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last six starts, Enchanted Lady has experience of today's trip and going but her recent finishes — seventh last time, ninth two starts back — make it hard to fancy her competitively off 136 lb from stall four, and our rating of 68 ranks her twelfth of seventeen.

runners_data.name: Lough Leane
runners_data.note: Tongue-tie worn; won at 10f on good last year and has a second placed run over 7f on good recently, so versatility over the ground is proven; at 32 days since last run freshness is acceptable, though his hold-up style means he'll need a gap to open in the straight that may simply not materialise given the volume of traffic.
runners_data.comment: Lough Leane landed a win four starts back and returns after a 32-day break with experience of today's trip and going in his favour, while our rating of 74 marks him out as a leading threat at the weights; the worry is his last three runs have yielded only a fourth.

runners_data.name: Showyoutheropes
runners_data.note: Visor worn; 10 of 13 similar-going runs show finishes of 4th or worse, which is a persistent under-performance flag on this ground; a hold-up type pushed toward midfield, and the headgear hasn't sparked a transformation in recent outings — hard to make a case for in this shape.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts, Showyoutheropes has at least shown experience over today's trip and conditions, and a speed rating of 76 offers modest encouragement, though a ninth last time out and stall seven from 136 lb make this a tough ask.

runners_data.name: Chosen One
runners_data.note: The youngest in the field at three and stepping back to 1m2½f from 10f — trips at which he ran 2nd and 6th on good; a hold-up horse showing a modest 0W1P from 4 qualifying runs on similar going; tongue-tie is noted, and his trainer's 14-day strike rate of 2/21 is modest without being alarming.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last five starts and ranked near the foot of our figures, Chosen One faces a stiff task here; second two starts back offers a crumb of comfort, and she has run over today's trip and going before, but 133 lb from stall 11 adds to the burden.

runners_data.name: Sweet Baby Zou
runners_data.note: Won at 10f on good and placed at 8f, so this 1m2½f trip is a slight stretch; flagged for fading in the finish, which is a meaningful concern if the gallop is moderate and the finale comes in a rush; hood worn, and the JP O'Brien yard has been in strong form (T14: 13/79 — solid volume and strike rate for a trainer in this sphere).
runners_data.comment: Sweet Baby Zou won one in her last six starts and ranks thirteenth of seventeen on our figures, making her hard to fancy at face value, though she was third last time out, has run over today's distance and going before, and returns on a fresh enough 14-day break.

runners_data.name: A Pretty Penny
runners_data.note: The race's only confirmed front-runner; two wins and two places over 10-12f on good ground in her last five outings, and dropping to a career-low OR of 64 off a light 128lbs; with Reserve 1 in the saddle the jockey angle is uncertain, but the tactical scenario of an uncontested lead on a flat track with good underfoot conditions is squarely in her favour.
runners_data.comment: Ranked bottom of the field on our figures, A Pretty Penny faces a stiff ask, though she does arrive on the back of a win last time out and has experience of today's distance and going; the 128 lb burden adds another complication.

runners_data.name: Good Man Jack
runners_data.note: Three-year-old flagged for fading in the finish; last five runs show finishes of 7th-17th and zero places from 5 qualifying runs on good ground — a deeply uninspiring recent profile; a genuine hold-up type mapped into midfield by congestion, and with Reserve 2 booked the jockey angle adds no encouragement.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts, with three finishes no better than seventh in that sequence, Good Man Jack is hard to fancy from stall nine off 128 lb, though he has run over today's trip and going before and returns on a quick eight-day turnaround.

runners_data.name: Chestnut Palace
runners_data.note: Hood worn; four consecutive 4th-place finishes tells you this horse is consistent but struggles to win — placed only 3 times in 6 good-ground runs; a prominent racer whose profile suits this pace shape in theory, and Noel Meade's yard has a 1/28 T14 strike — volume is there but the hit rate is modest.
runners_data.comment: Chestnut Palace has run over today's distance and going but remains winless in her last six starts, with a string of fourth and fifth placings suggesting she finds one or two too good; a yard in poor form and 86 days off the track are further concerns despite her rating of 73 offering some encouragement.

races.paceDynamic: A Pretty Penny is the lone confirmed front-runner in a 17-runner field and, with no genuine pace rival likely to challenge her for the lead, she should be allowed to dictate a controlled, sustainable gallop from the front over this 1m2½f trip on good ground. Hexagonal and Chestnut Palace will push up to track her from prominent positions, but neither is a tearaway type, so the tempo is unlikely to be frantic — a steady-to-moderate pace is the most probable shape. The field holds far more hold-up horses than the race shape can accommodate at the rear; Darkdeserthighway, Areana, Solomon, Berto Ramirez, Daonethatgotaway and several others are genuine hold-up types who will be forced closer to midfield than they would naturally choose, compressing the bunch and making a clean run in the straight far from guaranteed for closers. This race shape — a lone front-runner, steady gallop, compressed midfield — overwhelmingly favours those who can sit close to the pace and sustain their effort, meaning prominent racers and horses able to secure a tracking position behind A Pretty Penny hold a structural advantage over true come-from-behind types.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Lone Leader Controls
scenarios.trigger: If A Pretty Penny dictates an uncontested, measured gallop and kicks clear in the straight before the pack can organise.
scenarios.body: A Pretty Penny sets a comfortable pace, Hexagonal and Chestnut Palace cover her from close range but lack the acceleration to peg her back; the leader's recent course-distance form (1-2 in her last two at 12f on good) makes her dangerous off a light weight.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Pair Strike
scenarios.trigger: If the steady pace allows Hexagonal or Chestnut Palace to produce a sustained run from off the leader's shoulder entering the straight.
scenarios.body: A moderate tempo suits horses travelling comfortably just behind the pace rather than those trying to make ground from deep; Hexagonal's two wins at 10f on good and recent good form (601071) give him strong claims if he tracks A Pretty Penny throughout.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Midfield Mover Pounces
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is genuinely strong enough to compromise A Pretty Penny's stamina and a horse who has settled in midfield picks up the pieces late.
scenarios.body: A contested tempo would open a gap for a horse like Sinbad My Dad or Doctor Grace — both with proven form at this trip on good ground — to arrive with a late run; however, with the pace essentially uncontested this shape is structurally unlikely.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Closers Sweep Late
scenarios.trigger: If the field bunches badly and a late-developing hold-up horse finds a clear run to finish past a tiring field.
scenarios.body: True hold-up horses are oversubscribed and many are racing out of their natural position mapped to midfield; the compressed traffic makes a clear run for any genuine closer difficult to engineer, making this the least likely shape despite the large field.

watchPoints.text: A Pretty Penny is the only confirmed pace-setter in a 17-runner field — if she gets a clean break and no rival follows her up, she could control this race entirely unchallenged and be very difficult to peg back over 1m2½f on good ground.

Hexagonal is the prominent racer most likely to secure a prime tracking position behind A Pretty Penny; his tongue-tie, recent winning form and strong similar-going record (9/15, 2W3P) mean if he travels comfortably in second or third he becomes a serious danger in the straight.

With nine or more genuine hold-up horses competing for a limited number of rear berths, significant traffic congestion in the back straight and around the home turn is likely — watch for horses being switched wide or pocketed as the field compresses entering the final furlong.

Sweet Baby Zou is flagged for fading in the finish and is stepping beyond her proven trip of 10f — if JP O'Brien's yard has her cherry-ripe (T14: 13/79 is active form) she could be prominent early through the hood, but the stamina query over 1m2½f is real.

Sinbad My Dad ran just 12 days ago and placed at 11f on good last time — among the hold-up brigade he carries arguably the freshest and most relevant recent form, and should be monitored for how cleanly he gets a run in the straight from a midfield position.

races.name: Grant Thornton Handicap (Div I)

runners_data.name: Miss Australie
runners_data.note: Won over 14f on Good ground 8 days ago in sharp form, natural hold-up horse who stays well; the trip is fine but she needs a stronger pace than Coul Dore is expected to provide to generate her finish.
runners_data.comment: Miss Australie won last time out and has experience of today's trip and conditions, with a speed rating of 70 lending further weight to her claims; the concern is that she carries 148 lb on just an eight-day turnaround.

runners_data.name: Plains Indian
runners_data.note: Ten-year-old returning after a 445-day absence which is a major concern; a hold-up type who handles Good ground and stays marathon trips, but the layoff makes fitness deeply uncertain.

runners_data.name: God Of Thunder
runners_data.note: Wearing a tongue-tie here and placed over 18f recently suggesting stamina is a strong suit; a genuine hold-up horse who handles this going, though trainer's recent form (1/28 T14) is modest and he needs luck in running from the rear.
runners_data.comment: God Of Thunder has run over today's trip and going, and a rating of 64 — ranking him third of seventeen — marks him as a live threat on his best form; yet he arrives winless in his last six starts and his trainer is striking at just four per cent recently, which is the concern.

runners_data.name: Vervain
runners_data.note: Placed over 12f on Good ground twice this season and the step up to 1m5f looks like it suits; a hold-up type wearing a tongue-tie, has consistency in these conditions and could be better placed than many in a compressed midfield.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last five starts, Vervain does bring distance and going experience to the table, and her second two starts back shows she can get involved, but carrying 137 lb looks a stiff task for a filly rated 55.

runners_data.name: Maxwell Smart
runners_data.note: Placed three times over 14f on Good ground so the trip and going are squarely in his wheelhouse; his true style is hold-up but he has been mapped to midfield as this field cannot accommodate every rear-runner, tempering confidence in him landing his ideal race shape.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last six starts, Maxwell Smart does at least bring distance and going experience to the table, and a third two starts back hints at some residual ability; however, the weight of 132 lb and a modest official rating of 50 suggest he faces a stiff task from the middle of the pack.

runners_data.name: Limestone Red
runners_data.note: Placed twice over 12f on Good ground, but the jump to 1m5f is a question he has not yet answered; runs from the back by nature but the crowded hold-up department in this race means he may be forced closer than ideal, which does not play to his strengths.
runners_data.comment: Limestone Red arrives here on the back of consecutive placed efforts — third last time out and a runner-up two starts back — showing he's in decent nick after 20 days off, and having experience of today's trip and conditions is a clear asset; the concern is that his official mark of 47 leaves him carrying 129 lb.

runners_data.name: No More Hiding
runners_data.note: Carries a fading-in-finish flag and a step up to 1m5f from shorter trips is a significant stamina test for a three-year-old; a genuine hold-up type by nature but among those most likely to actually secure a forward position given the congested rear of the field.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last five starts, No More Hiding arrives here 23 days on from a fifth-place effort, and while she has run over today's going before, a rating of 55 ranking her seventh of seventeen suggests she faces a stiff task to make a breakthrough.

runners_data.name: Quinchy Lady
runners_data.note: Only three career runs and all over shorter trips, so this 1m5f trip into a 17-runner handicap represents a sharp step up in both distance and depth; a hold-up type but form figures show she has not threatened a placing yet.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last three starts and ranked near the foot of the field on our figures, Quinchy Lady faces a stiff task here, though she does return on a surface she has encountered before and is at least fit on 21 days since her last outing.

runners_data.name: Invincible Destiny
runners_data.note: Yet to finish closer than seventh in four runs and fades in finishes, which is a recurring concern; naturally runs from the rear but with so many hold-up types in the field she is unlikely to find the clean passage she needs, and the form book does not inspire.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last four starts and ranked last of the field on our figures, Invincible Destiny faces a stiff task under 127 lb for a trainer in poor form; experience over today's trip and going is the main saving grace.

runners_data.name: Money Shuffler
runners_data.note: Wears a hood and has finished out of the first six in every recent start; a true hold-up horse mapped to midfield by necessity, carries a fading flag, and the Good ground form is thin over this kind of trip.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last five starts, Money Shuffler does at least have experience over today's trip and a our rating of 55 suggests more ability than her official mark of 45 implies, though her recent string of unplaced efforts makes confidence hard to justify.

runners_data.name: Coul Dore
runners_data.note: The lone front-runner in the race and the key pace-setter; wears headgear combination (hood and tongue-tie) and showed when second over 10f on Good ground, but the fading-in-finish flag and step up to 1m5f raise genuine stamina doubts about whether she can sustain her lead all the way.
runners_data.comment: Coul Dore arrives here 20 days fresh and has going experience to call on, but he is winless in his last five starts, with a second three starts back the only bright spot in a patchy recent record, and a rating of 52 leaves him well down the 17-runner field.

runners_data.name: Piatra Neamt
runners_data.note: Placed over 14f on Good ground and seems to stay, wearing a hood; but a hold-up runner forced forward by the weight of closers in this field, and recent form figures are uninspiring with no win or place on Good ground in six attempts.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last five starts, with a string of unplaced efforts and only a fifth two starts back to show, Piatra Neamt is hard to fancy at the foot of the ratings, though she has run over today's distance and going before and returns on a manageable 30-day break.

runners_data.name: Princess Rosie
runners_data.note: Five runs all on Good ground and all over shorter 7f-10f trips, so this 1m5f trip is a major stamina question; a natural hold-up type mapped towards the midfield here, and the form figures (multiple last-place finishes) make it hard to be positive.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last five starts, Princess Rosie at least has experience of today's going in her favour, though her record of unplaced efforts and two mid-division finishes suggests she faces a stiff task against stronger rivals from her ranking of tenth of seventeen.

runners_data.name: Flagstone Lady
runners_data.note: Third over 12f on Good ground four days ago — that recent run gives her a fitness edge — and the form shows some promise; a hold-up horse by nature but one of several pushed closer than ideal, though the very recent outing (4 days) may benefit her.
runners_data.comment: Flagstone Lady has run over today's trip and going, and that third last time out shows she can find the frame, though she is winless in her last six starts and a return to form four days on from that effort asks questions of her stamina for the contest.

runners_data.name: Jazz Forever
runners_data.note: Prominent-running type with experience over similar trips, placed over 13f on Good ground; ridden by Reserve 1 which introduces a minor jockey uncertainty, but the style is ideally suited to tracking Coul Dore and pouncing.
runners_data.comment: Jazz Forever has run over today's trip and going, and returns on a quick eight-day turnaround, but three consecutive unplaced efforts weigh against him and he remains winless in his last six starts, making it hard to fancy him with confidence from a mark of 51.

runners_data.name: Lariat
runners_data.note: Ten-year-old veteran who has placed twice over 16f on Good ground; a genuine prominent type who handles this trip well, and despite being ridden by Reserve 2, his tactical position close to the pace suits the likely race shape better than most.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts, with finishes of seventh or worse in three of those, Lariat is hard to fancy on these figures despite a second two starts back and some experience over today's trip and going.

runners_data.name: Premier Princess
runners_data.note: Fades in finishes and has not placed on Good ground in five attempts; a hold-up type by nature but among those most likely to be pushed forward in this congested field — trainer Hogan also saddles God Of Thunder, splitting stable interest.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last five starts and ranked 13 of 17 on our figures, Premier Princess has little in her favour beyond distance and going experience; a trainer striking at just 4% recently and a return just four days ago make her hard to fancy here.

races.paceDynamic: Coul Dore is the sole confirmed front-runner in a 17-horse field and, with no genuine rival to push the pace, is set to bowl along uncontested on the front end over this 1m5f trip on Good ground at Down Royal. Jazz Forever and Lariat will press from prominent positions but neither is a natural leader, so Coul Dore should control the fractions and set a sustainable, metronomic gallop rather than a searching one. With the pace modest and predictable, horses that can travel close to the speed without expending energy — prominent and midfield stalkers — are best placed to pounce, whereas true closers need a strong early tempo to generate the finish they require, and that tempo simply will not be supplied here. This field contains a glut of genuine hold-up horses — including No More Hiding, Invincible Destiny, Premier Princess, Money Shuffler, Piatra Neamt, Princess Rosie and Flagstone Lady — who cannot all find the rear of the field they prefer and several will be forced to race closer than ideal; of those, No More Hiding and Premier Princess are most likely to actually secure a forward berth given their handlers' tactical flexibility.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Coul Dore Controls Uncontested
scenarios.trigger: If Coul Dore dictates a modest, uncontested gallop and kicks on turning in before hold-up horses can close.
scenarios.body: Coul Dore sets a comfortable pace throughout, conserving enough energy to sustain the run-in; the field strings out as closers struggle to generate momentum from too far back against a controlled tempo.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Stalkers Pounce
scenarios.trigger: If Jazz Forever or Lariat track Coul Dore closely and overhaul the leader in the straight as the front-runner fades.
scenarios.body: The modest pace suits horses travelling prominent without burning resources early, and the straight at Down Royal provides enough length for a stalker to collar a tiring leader; Jazz Forever's experience over similar trips and ground makes this a live threat.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Midfield Runner Swoops
scenarios.trigger: If the pace proves just brisk enough to string the field and a well-placed midfield horse picks off a weakening leader.
scenarios.body: A runner like Vervain or God Of Thunder, sitting a few lengths off the pace in mid-division, finds room on the outer turning for home and sustains a run to the line; this scenario requires Coul Dore to fade earlier than expected, opening a gap for a horse with a touch more stamina.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Late Closers Swamp Field
scenarios.trigger: If Coul Dore goes too fast early and the field compresses late, allowing genuine back-markers to finish powerfully.
scenarios.body: This requires a materially stronger early pace than Coul Dore appears likely to set, and many of the true hold-up types in this field are redistributed out of their natural position and carry fading-in-finish flags; the conditions for a mass late swoop are unlikely to materialise.

watchPoints.text: Coul Dore's stamina over 1m5f is unproven — watch whether she begins to shorten stride entering the final two furlongs, as any sign of weakening opens the race up immediately for Jazz Forever and Lariat.

With at least seven genuine hold-up horses unable to find the rear, there is a significant risk of crowding and checking on the first bend as runners jostle for position — watch the draw and early positioning closely.

Jazz Forever and Lariat are ridden by Reserve 1 and Reserve 2 jockeys respectively — if the listed jockeys are replaced closer to race time, reassess tactical intentions as unfamiliar combinations can misread a race at a crucial moment.

Flagstone Lady ran just four days ago and Coul Dore eight days ago — both are on short turnarounds; monitor markets for any late market moves suggesting stable confidence or trainer concern about bounce effect.

Plains Indian has not raced for 445 days and faces a sharp fitness test; if he is well-backed despite the layoff it suggests connections have done significant homework at home, but form-book punters should treat him with caution.

races.name: Grant Thornton Handicap (Div II)

runners_data.name: Charlie Brow'n
runners_data.note: Won at 14f on Soft 14 days ago for O'Mara and Lordan — yard out of recent form (0/4 T14) but the horse arrives here in form; a genuine hold-up runner whose Good-ground similar-distance record (1 win, 1 placed from 7) is modest, and this drop from a win may bring a penalty burden; must hope the pace collapse scenario materialises.
runners_data.comment: Third last time out gives Charlie Brow'n a recent near-miss to build on, but a seventh two starts back suggests inconsistency; he has run over today's trip and going, carries 141 lb, and our rating of 58 leaves him with something to find against the principals.

runners_data.name: Spy
runners_data.note: Seven-year-old veteran with 2 wins and 5 places from 12 similar-going runs — course-proven but shows a patchy record at 17f on Good; visor fitted, and Bryan's yard has been in good nick (1/7 T14); a deep closer who needs the race to set up for him, which this controlled pace shape may not.
runners_data.comment: Spy won two starts back and has experience of both today's trip and going, arriving here on a fresh 17-day break carrying 141 lb — the main concern is that unplaced effort last time out, which he will need to put firmly behind him.

runners_data.name: Tassarolo
runners_data.note: Hogan-trained five-year-old fitted with tongue-strap who has finished 3rd–5th in most recent runs — consistent enough but has never won on Good ground at this trip; 20 days since last run is fine, and the 17f placing in hist gives confidence on the stamina question; hold-up style means he needs something to go wrong up front.
runners_data.comment: Tassarolo is winless in his last six starts, though a third three starts back offers some encouragement; he returns after 20 days and has run over today's trip and going, but 140 lb and a trainer firing at just 4% in the last fortnight are notable drags.

runners_data.name: Dancing Steve
runners_data.note: The sole confirmed pace-setter, making him the most tactically important horse in the race even at a modest OR of 56; his profile warns of fading in the finish and his recent form over shorter trips (9–10f) raises questions about whether he truly gets 1m5f; visor worn, and McGuinness's yard has been busy (4/32 T14).
runners_data.comment: Placed third last time out on a quick turnaround of 20 days, Dancing Steve arrives with some fitness in his favour and has run over today's trip and going before, though he carries 138 lb and has been winless in his last five starts, limiting optimism from seventh in the ratings.

runners_data.name: Acanto
runners_data.note: Meade's four-year-old has only three career runs, all on different going types — a genuinely unexposed profile, but the limited data (0 wins, 0 places from 3 similar-going runs) makes evaluation difficult; a true hold-up runner whose natural station is at the rear, though in this congested field he is likely squeezed closer to midfield than he would prefer.
runners_data.comment: Rated well clear of her mark and ranked second in the field on our figures, Acanto has run over today's trip and going and returns after a 35-day break with fresh legs; yet to score in her last three starts, and a trainer running at just 4% makes confidence harder to hold.

runners_data.name: Mullacurry Maid
runners_data.note: Kinsella filly with a fading-in-finish flag and a record showing 0 wins and 0 places from 3 similar-going runs — has shown enough to suggest she handles Good ground but not enough to suggest she wins here; her natural instinct to race from the back is further compromised by the crowded nature of this field.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last five starts and ranked 15th of 17 on our figures, Mullacurry Maid faces a stiff task here, though she does return on a quick turnaround with going experience in her favour and at least arrives fit.

runners_data.name: Rio Doce
runners_data.note: 84 days off the track is a notable fitness concern, and the 0/4 T14 yard stat adds doubt; fitted with tongue-strap and pads, and while the form at 16f–18f on Good shows some staying ability, finishing positions of 13th and 14th feature prominently; a genuine hold-up type who needs a strong pace to close into, which is unlikely here.
runners_data.comment: Rio Doce is winless in his last five starts, with a fourth three starts back the brightest note in a patchy recent sequence, and 84 days off the track raises a fitness query under 133 lb, though he has run over today's trip and going before.

runners_data.name: Mapa

races.paceDynamic: Dancing Steve is the sole confirmed front runner in this 17-runner field over 1m5f on Good ground at Down Royal, and with no identified rival willing to press him hard from the off, he is likely to dictate a controlled, sustainable gallop through the early stages. That uncontested lead creates a race where the pace is unlikely to be truly searching, which historically at this trip favours horses who can race prominently or within a few lengths of the pace rather than those forced to make up a significant deficit late. The cluster of genuine hold-up horses — Charlie Brow'n, Spy, Tassarolo, Connecteo, and Zitkala Sa among them — will need the gallop to quicken and string the field out in the final two furlongs to deliver their challenge, but the moderate tempo Dancing Steve will likely set risks leaving too much to do for true back-markers. This race shape most favours prominent racers or hold-up horses with the tactical speed to position themselves within striking range by the home turn, not horses relying on a deep closing burst off a slow pace. Note that this field holds considerably more genuine hold-up types than the map's midfield band can physically accommodate — Queen Of Astolat, Acanto, Rio Doce, Mapa, and several others are natural back-markers who will struggle to achieve their preferred closer's role and may find themselves further back than ideal.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Controlled Lead, Front Finishes
scenarios.trigger: If Dancing Steve dictates an honest but uncontested gallop and the field strings out behind him without a late surge.
scenarios.body: Dancing Steve sets a comfortable tempo and those positioned close to him, such as Connecteo and Zitkala Sa, are able to track and pounce in the straight without facing a wall of horses; a non-punishing pace rewards horses who travel sweetly through the race rather than grinding from the rear.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse, Late Rush
scenarios.trigger: If Dancing Steve fades badly in the straight — as his profile warns — and the tempo was only moderate enough to set up a sprint finish for closers.
scenarios.body: With the front runner stopping sharply, genuine hold-up horses who managed to get a position closer to midfield than their natural station, such as Charlie Brow'n and Spy, are best placed to pick up the pieces; Spy's course-form at this trip on Good ground and Charlie Brow'n's recent win on Soft at 14f give both relevance if the race turns into a final-furlong dash.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Grind Test, Stayers Prevail
scenarios.trigger: If a slightly stronger gallop develops — perhaps from early crowding in a 17-runner field — and the race becomes a true test of stamina over the final three furlongs.
scenarios.body: Horses with proven form at 1m4f–1m6f on Good ground, who can travel economically before grinding their rivals down, benefit most; Tassarolo's placed efforts at 17f and Rio Doce's history at 16f–18f on Good give them each a stamina edge, though Rio Doce's long absence and STYLE_FIT concern temper expectations.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Wide Draw, Traffic Chaos
scenarios.trigger: If the large field causes severe traffic issues in the final bend, benefitting those on the outer or with clear runs over the final two furlongs.
scenarios.body: In a 17-runner handicap, horses trapped wide early may actually secure better positions rounding the home turn and avoid the bunching that will inevitably trap several of the redistributed hold-up types; Connecteo's recent sharp form and Queen Of Astolat's consistent placed efforts in similar Good-ground 1m4f races give both an angle if they secure daylight.

watchPoints.text: Dancing Steve's stamina is unproven at 1m5f and his recent runs over 9–10f combined with the fading-in-finish flag mean he could stop very quickly from the two-furlong pole — watch whether he is passed in a rush in the home straight, as this will compress the entire race outcome into a short finale.

With 17 runners, the home turn at Down Royal is likely to cause significant bunching — watch for Queen Of Astolat, Acanto, and Rio Doce, all genuine hold-up types compressed into midfield, potentially finding themselves blocked and unable to produce their challenge at the critical moment.

Duleek Street's 397-day absence is the longest in the field by far — watch the market to gauge stable confidence, and monitor his early position; if he is struggling by halfway, he may create interference for closers tracking him.
